Did this run OK on Jenkins? If so, then I wonder if
there's a specific compiler or optimization level that
causes this.

The easy fix is to get rid of the exception in the destructor.
And make it non-virtual at the same time so there's no
additional overhead.

Can I reply to these messages that seem to arise from
GitHub? I just pasted in stan-dev instead on this one.

- Bob

parts: On Sun, Feb 10, 2013 at 5:19 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

Did this run OK on Jenkins?   If so, then I wonder if
there's a specific compiler or optimization level that
causes this.
No, it didn't run ok on Jenkins. That's how I found this issue. (I had to do a little more work to get the error message propagated -- some oddness in how I was using google test.)

The easy fix is to get rid of the exception in the destructor.
And make it non-virtual at the same time so there's no
additional overhead.

That's one way to fix it. Is there any bad behavior associated with allowing the destructor be called automatically? I didn't work through all the conditions and whether or not having the destructor be called automatically was indeed an error.

Can I reply to these messages that seem to arise from
GitHub?  I just pasted in stan-dev instead on this one.
I believe you can. In doing so, you'll update the issue itself. At least, that's what the documentation says.

parts:
On 2/10/13 7:12 PM, bgoodri wrote:
> For some reason, I can't even cross-compile mvn_orange any more:
>
> --- Translating Stan graphical model to C++ code ---
> bin/stanc.exe models/bugs_examples/vol2/mvn_orange/mvn_orange.stan --o=models/bugs_examples/vol2/mvn_orange/mvn_orange.cpp
> bin/stanc.exe: 1: bin/stanc.exe: MZ����@���: not found
> bin/stanc.exe: 2: bin/stanc.exe: Syntax error: "|" unexpected
>
> So, I can't look at it under gdb.
>
> Anyway, we should git bisect this on Windows. Write a script that just does
>
> 1. make clean-all
> 2. make models/bugs_examples/vol2/mvn_orange/mvn_orange
> 3. executes mvn_orange.exe
> 4. returns the return code from mvn_orange.exe which is zero iff successful
>
> Then, in a tree without uncommitted stuff, do
>
> 1. git bisect start
> 2. git bisect good v1.1.0 # presuming it was working correctly then
> 3. git bisect bad HEAD
> 4. git bisect run myscript.exe
>
> I'm guessing this problem was caused or exposed when Marcus refactored multi_normal() to use more varis.

I'm sure that's what the problem is. Daniel and
I were complicit in that refactoring, and it seems
to work OK on Jenkins.

There's an easy fix by not having the destructor
throw an exception. It shouldn't be getting called,
but apparently sometimes it is. Maybe something I
inadvertently put on the call stack (as opposed to our
stack).

- Bob
